[P2] Synchronize losing steps with the batch decision

If the first checkpoint response takes longer than 200 ms, items 1–3 enqueue their `SUCCEED` updates before item 0 finishes its awaited checkpoint and closes the batch gate. Closing the gate does not remove queued updates, so a correct execution records additional `StepSucceeded` events, whereas both new history fixtures require only one. The cloud tests can therefore fail solely because of checkpoint latency and miss the intended dropped-checkpoint scenario. Replace the fixed sleep with a signal that releases the losing steps after the batch decision; the slow-serdes case can release it from the winning item's deserializer.
